reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no counterparty comment, which is the expected output shape for a clause sitting at the fallback; nothing was proposed that could over-flag or mis-edit the text.

The cited text supports the classification: §4(a) gives either Party a no-cause right ('terminate this Agreement for any reason') after a 1-year Initial Term on ninety (90) days' notice, which lands inside the fallback's 60–90 day Customer notice window and outside walk-away territory (Vendor notice is exactly 90 days, not fewer).

The T4C detection trigger for a missing Customer convenience right requires a committed term longer than 12 months; the Initial Term is exactly one year with 1-year auto-renewals, and the mid-Initial-Term bar is symmetric (it equally locks Kubient in), so it is not adverse to us.

No early-termination penalty is imposed on the Customer — Kubient is entitled only to fees 'generated during the termination period' (i.e., earned while performing through the 90-day notice), well within the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling, and the revenue-share structure means the Customer prepays no refundable fees.

The failed deterministic check is credibly reconciled: the regex looks for literal 'for convenience' wording and misses the equivalent 'for any reason' formulation, so it is a phrasing variant rather than a substantive gap.

Residual gaps (90-day rather than 30-day Customer notice, no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, and Kubient's convenience right not confined to the end of a renewal term) are correctly recorded as sub-elements short of the preferred position rather than escalated; the last of these is the closest call, but with 90 days' notice and a rolling 1-year term it does not defeat the fallback on a material term.
